description: Links two thoughts. Call it when you spot a meaningful relationship between existing thoughts — links are what make a brain a graph rather than a list. Label the link via name: "motivates", "solved by", "contradicts". Two thoughts share one link: where one joins them already nothing is added, and the result says what is there.

brainId.description: Brain identifier. Take it from brain_list — never guess it.

name.description: Link label: how exactly one relates to the other.

relation.description: How the target relates to the source. Defaults to jump — a sideways link that leaves the hierarchy alone. Siblings are not linked to each other: they are thoughts with a parent in common. A type cannot be the parent: that link would set the child's type, which is what typeId of brain_update_thought is for. Nor can a tag: that link would tag the child, which is what brain_tag is for.

replace.description: Make a link of another kind that joins the two into this one: a jump into a parent-child link, or the other end above. It keeps its identifier, and its label unless name gives one. Never a tag or a type.

name: brain_link
